cards.text: The LORD is still answering Habakkuk the prophet, who asked why God is silent while the wicked swallow up those more righteous than themselves (Habakkuk 1:13). God has just described the proud one, an arrogant man who gathers all the nations to himself like he's collecting stickers (Habakkuk 2:5). Now God says those nations will take up a taunt against him, and friend, a taunt is NOT a thank-you card.

cards.question: The nations' taunt starts with 'Woe to him who amasses what is not his…' What else does the proud one use to make himself rich?

cards.text: And the taunt has a question in it: 'How long will this go on?' Friend, I asked that exact question from the back of a junk drawer for YEARS.

cards.question: True or false: God says the proud man's creditors will forget about everything he owes them.

cards.text: His creditors will suddenly arise, and he'll become their prey. That's the guy who borrowed twenty bucks from every coworker, walks into the break room, and EVERYBODY looks up at once.

cards.question: God says the remnant of the people will turn on the proud man and take his riches. Why?

answers.text: Because he refused to pay tribute

cards.text: He spilled blood and brought violence on the land, the city and everyone living there. And now, here comes woe number two.

cards.question: The second woe is for the man who builds his house by ___ gain.
The man in the second woe builds his house and places his nest up high. What does he hope to escape up there?

cards.text: But all that climbing backfires. God says he's plotted shame for his own house by cutting off many peoples and forfeiting his own life.

cards.question: God says the house this man built will tell on him: the ___ will cry out from the wall.

cards.text: The stones will cry out from the wall, and the rafters will echo it from the woodwork. Friend, when I sneak a cookie off the cooling rack, the crumbs in my mustache tell on me EVERY single time.

cards.question: True or false: The third woe is for the man who builds a city with bloodshed.

cards.text: Then God asks: isn't it from the LORD of Hosts that the people's labor only feeds the fire, and the nations wear themselves out for nothing? That's decorating a whole batch for hours and then leaving the tray in the oven ALL NIGHT.

cards.question: The labor of the people only feeds the fire. God goes on to say the earth will be filled with something. What is it?

answers.text: The knowledge of the LORD's glory
The songs of the freed nations
The gold of the fallen cities

cards.text: As the waters cover the sea, that's how full the earth will be. Not a little spill on the counter, friend, the WHOLE SEA.
Woe number four is for him who gives drink to his neighbors, pouring it from the wineskin until they are drunk, in order to gaze at their nakedness.

cards.question: The fourth woe is for a man who gets his neighbors drunk. God says he will be filled with something instead of glory. What is it?

cards.text: So God turns it around. Now he too must drink and expose his uncircumcision.

cards.question: The proud man poured drink for others, but now the cup in the ___ right hand will come around to him.

cards.text: Utter disgrace will cover his glory. And God isn't finished naming what this man has done.

cards.question: God tells the proud man that his violence against one place will overwhelm him. Which place?
True or false: God says the destruction of animals will terrify the proud man.

cards.text: All because of his bloodshed against men and his violence against the land, the city and everyone living there. Then God asks what use an idol is, that a craftsman should carve it.

cards.question: God calls the idol a teacher of lies and says its maker trusts in his own creation. What kind of idols does he make?

cards.text: Woe number five is for him who says to wood, 'Awake!' or to silent stone, 'Arise!' That's me yelling 'GET UP!' at my wooden rolling pin, friend, and it has NEVER rolled itself one time.

cards.question: True or false: Even with all its gold and silver, the idol has breath in it.

cards.text: Shiny gold and silver, and no breath in it at all. But the LORD is a whole different story.

cards.question: The idol can't give guidance and has no breath. But where is the LORD?
The LORD is in His holy temple. What should all the earth do before Him?

cards.text: Let that quiet sit a minute, friend. Trust me, Habakkuk's story isn't over yet.
